title: The Barrow Feast
text: A barrow door stands open on a hall laid for a feast. The dead sit at the table in their rotted finery, cups raised to a toast that never ended. There is one empty place among them, set fresh, the bread still warm.

options.label: The Leader takes the empty place at the table, so as not to insult the dead.

outcomes.text: The dead drink to the living all night, laughing without breath, and give a gift at parting.
The place was set for someone who meant to stay. The Leader's eyes grow heavy, and the dead lean closer, smiling.

options.label: Raise a cup from the doorway, and go before anyone asks you to sit.

outcomes.text: They raise theirs back, all of them, with a creak of old bones, and the door swings gently shut.

options.label: Take the silver off the table. The dead have no use for it.

outcomes.text: The dead stand up, all at once, cups still in their hands. They do use it, it seems.
